Pediatric cancer demands relentless focus on breaking barriers to treatment innovation. The Give Kids a Chance Act (H.R.1262) directly confronts systemic failures in drug development by mandating pediatric studies for molecularly targeted therapies and novel drug combinations—critical when 70% of childhood cancer survivors face lifelong complications from outdated treatments. This bill’s reauthorization of priority review vouchers until 2029 forces Big Pharma to redirect profits toward rare pediatric diseases instead of abandoning smaller markets.

Roswell Park’s advocacy underscores the urgency: 16,000 kids diagnosed annually can’t wait for D.C.’s bureaucratic pace. While the legislation cracks open doors for combination trials, real accountability lies in enforcing PREA deadlines and crushing Pharma’s loopholes that delay pediatric data submissions.

Progress hinges on bills like this bridging the gap between adult and pediatric research—but only if implemented without letting regulators cave to industry pressure.
